items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No

02. I understand that my application will be considered incomplete if any required sections of the application are not completed and/or if any documents that are required are not attached to my online application by the closing date. Options: Yes | No
03. Please specify your highest level of education. Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree

04. Do you have a bachelor's degree or higher in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Industrial/Organizational Development, or a closely related field? Options: No | Yes, I have a bachelor's degree in one of the specified fields or a closely related field. | Yes, I have a master's degree or higher in one of the specified fields or a closely related field.
05. Please indicate the field in which you have earned your degree in:

06. Please indicate the full-time equivalent years of progressively responsible, professional human resources experience. Options: No experience | One year | Two years | Three years | Four years | Five years | Six years | Seven years | Eight years | Nine years | Ten or more years

07. Please indicate the full-time equivalent years of experience in a supervisory or managerial capacity overseeing HR staff or functions. Options: No experience | One year | Two years | Three years | Four years | Five years or more

08. Please indicate where you obtained at least: Five (5) years of progressively responsible, professional human resources experience and three (3) years of experience in a supervisory or managerial capacity overseeing HR staff or functions. 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed. (This section is required)
09. Do you possess a professional Human Resources (HR) certification, such as a PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, or equivalent? Options: Yes | No
10. If you selected "Yes" to the previous question, please specify the professional HR certification(s) you currently hold. If you selected "No," please enter "N/A."
11. Do you have prior human resources experience within a California Community College District employment environment? Options: Yes | No

12. If you selected "Yes" to the previous question, please describe your human resources experience within a California Community College District. If you selected "No," please enter "N/A." 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

13. Which of the following best describes your experience overseeing human resources operations, including recruitment and selection, employee relations, benefits administration, staff development, policy development, and supervision of HR personnel? Options: No experience overseeing human resources operations. | Limited experience assisting with or coordinating human resources operations. | Experience directly managing one or two human resources functions, such as recruitment, employee relations, or benefits administration. | Substantial experience managing several human resources functions, including supervising staff and implementing operational or procedural improvements. | Extensive experience directing comprehensive human resources operations, including multiple HR functions, staff supervision, strategic planning, policy development, and operational improvements.

14. Which of the following best describes your experience in labor-management relations, including collective bargaining, contract interpretation, grievance administration, and employee disciplinary matters? Options: No experience in labor-management relations or collective bargaining. | Limited experience assisting with labor relations activities, contract interpretation, or grievance administration. | Experience directly interpreting collective bargaining agreements or handling employee grievances and disciplinary matters. | Substantial experience managing labor relations matters, including contract administration, grievance resolution, employee discipline, and participation in collective bargaining negotiations. | Extensive experience leading labor-management relations, including collective bargaining negotiations, contract interpretation and administration, grievance resolution, and advising management on complex disciplinary and contractual matters.

15. If you indicated that you have experience in labor-management relations or collective bargaining, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

16. Which of the following best describes your experience conducting or overseeing workplace investigations involving discrimination, harassment, retaliation, employee misconduct, or other employment-related complaints, while ensuring compliance with applicable employment laws and regulations? Options: No experience conducting or overseeing workplace investigations. | Limited experience assisting with workplace investigations or employment-related compliance matters. | Experience directly conducting workplace investigations, gathering evidence, interviewing involved parties, or preparing investigative findings. | Substantial experience independently conducting complex workplace investigations, preparing written findings, and recommending appropriate actions in accordance with applicable employment laws and policies. | Extensive experience leading and overseeing complex workplace investigations, reviewing investigative findings, advising management on corrective actions, and collaborating with legal counsel to address employment law compliance and litigation risks.

17. If you indicated that you have experience conducting or overseeing workplace investigations, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

18. Which of the following best describes your experience developing, implementing, or overseeing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) programs, equitable recruitment and selection practices, and employment-related compliance training? Options: No experience with EEO programs or employment-related compliance training. | Limited experience assisting with EEO initiatives, equitable hiring practices, or compliance training. | Experience directly implementing EEO initiatives, supporting equitable recruitment and selection practices, or developing and delivering compliance training. | Substantial experience overseeing EEO initiatives, developing or implementing EEO plans, monitoring equitable employment practices, and coordinating compliance training. | Extensive experience directing comprehensive EEO programs, including developing, implementing, and monitoring EEO plans, leading EEO advisory committees or equivalent groups, overseeing equitable employment practices, and administering organization-wide compliance training.

19. If you indicated that you have experience developing, implementing, or overseeing EEO programs or employment-related compliance training, please provide the following information: 1. What was the time frame? 2. What was the employer's name? 3. Describe the work you performed.

20. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
Professional HR certification (e.g., PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP).
Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Industrial/Organizational Development, or a closely related field.
Master’s degree or Juris Doctor (J.D.) in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Industrial/Organizational Development, or a closely related field.
Five (5) years of progressively responsible, professional human resources experience.
Seven (7) or more years of professional human resources experience.

Demonstrated experience working with communities who have been traditionally underserved by higher education and experience in the pedagogy reflecting intersections of race, culture, class, ethnic, and queer communities.
Three (3) years of experience in a supervisory or managerial capacity overseeing HR staff or functions.
Prior human resources experience within a California Community College District employment environment.

Plans, organizes, and directs the day-to-day operations of the Human Resources Department, including employee relations, hiring, employee benefits, leaves, workers’ compensation, training and staff development, and policy development and review; establishes service standards and implements process and technology improvements that support District objectives.

Serves as the District’s Equal Employment Opportunity Officer; develops, maintains, and monitors the District’s EEO Plan in consultation with administration, faculty, staff, and shared governance groups, facilitates the EEO Advisory Committee, and ensures that EEO principles are applied across recruitment, selection, and other employment practices.

Oversees investigations of complaints of unlawful discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and workplace safety concerns; ensures compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Title VII, Title IX, the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), and related requirements, and prepares or reviews findings and written reports.

Assumes primary responsibility for employee disciplinary matters and grievance processes; advises managers, supervisors, and employees on District policies, performance evaluation, progressive discipline, contractual provisions, and the California Education Code, and investigates and prepares written responses to grievances filed under collective bargaining agreements.

Develops and coordinates the collection and analysis of data used in collective bargaining; participates in negotiations and contract administration; interprets collective bargaining agreements, Memoranda of Understanding, administrative procedures, and board policies, and acts as the District’s negotiator in the Assistant Superintendent, Vice President’s absence or as assigned.

Directs the District’s employee leave and integrated disability management programs, including the interactive process, reasonable accommodations, return-to-work, and workers’ compensation claims administration, ensuring compliance with applicable leave laws and District obligations.

Directly manages all aspects of the employee lifecycle including recruitment, transfers, suspensions, layoffs, recalls, promotions, terminations, task assignments, performance evaluations, rewards, disciplinary actions, and grievance resolution, ensuring adherence to District policies and legal requirements.

Works with District management, bargaining unit representatives, and legal counsel to identify and resolve compliance and risk issues related to leaves, unlawful discrimination, workplace safety, workers’ compensation, subpoenas, and payroll; manages annual state and federal employment posting requirements and serves as District liaison to external agencies and governmental units.

Assesses District training needs and ensures implementation of a comprehensive compliance and EEO training program, including training for selection committees on EEO, diversity in hiring, unlawful discrimination, and sexual harassment prevention.

Assists the Assistant Superintendent, Vice President, Human Resources with strategic planning, budget forecasting, and administration of the departmental budget; directs the preparation of staff reports, studies, and analyses, recommends new or revised human resources policies and procedures, and participates in shared governance committees, task forces, and Board of Trustees meetings as assigned.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Five (5) years in a supervisory or managerial capacity overseeing HR staff or functions.
Capacity to identify compliance and litigation risks in the workplace and recommend sound, legally defensible courses of action.

Thorough understanding of labor-management relations under the Educational Employment Relations Act (EERA), including collective bargaining, contract interpretation, grievance administration, and Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) processes.
Familiarity with workplace investigation methods, evidentiary standards, and report writing for discrimination, harassment, and misconduct complaints.

Knowledge of federal, state, and local employment law applicable to California community colleges, including the California Education Code, Government Code, Title 5, FEHA, ADA, FMLA/CFRA, Title VII, and Title IX.
Skill in analyzing complex personnel and compliance data and preparing clear narrative and statistical reports, studies, and recommendations.
Knowledge of Title 5 Equal Employment Opportunity Plan requirements and practices that promote diversity and equity in recruitment, selection, and retention.
Proficient in designing and delivering training and presenting proposals and technical information to managers, employee groups, and governance bodies.
Working knowledge of public administration principles, including budgeting, risk management, records retention, and human resources information systems.
Skill in mediation and conflict resolution, applying neutrality, discretion, and confidentiality to sensitive personnel matters.
Ability to plan, organize, and direct a comprehensive human resources program, setting priorities and timelines that ensure timely resolution of personnel matters.
Ability to interpret, apply, and explain laws, collective bargaining agreements, board policies, and administrative procedures to managers and employees.
Ability to select, supervise, train, and evaluate staff and foster a service-oriented, high-performing team.
Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with bargaining unit leadership, shared governance groups, legal counsel, and external agencies.
